mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns remains positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE decreases > 0.5pp, or if the correlation between UNRATE decreases and SPX returns remains positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS increases, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and SPX returns remains negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which can lead to increased corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO increases > 1%, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns remains negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k & UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS and UNRATE meet the trigger conditions, or if the joint correlation remains negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in housing starts (HOUST) signals a weakening demand for new homes, which can lead to a slowdown in related industries and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when HOUST decreases > 10%, or if the correlation between HOUST decreases and SPX returns remains positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary pressures, which can lead to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases > 2%, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and SPX returns remains positive over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, especially in a low-interest-rate environment.
regime_hint: early-cycle expansion with accommodative monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 and FEDFUNDS meet the trigger conditions, or if the joint correlation remains negative over a 3-year rolling window.
